---
title: "A single renv project can pile up several libraries depending on R and the platform"
ref: RNV-07
categories: [renv and installation]
impact: cryptique
attendu: "a single library, the project's"
versions: "All versions of {renv}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2021)"
---

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```text
renv/library/
├── R-4.0/
│   └── x86_64-w64-mingw32/
└── R-4.1/
    └── x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/
```
:::

This pitfall depends on several R installations and a Docker container, so it cannot be replayed in the browser.

## Why

{renv} stores the project library in a subfolder specific to the minor R version and the platform. This is by design: a package compiled for R 4.0 on Windows does not work on Linux.

When the same folder is used locally and then in a Docker container mounted as a volume, or after an R upgrade, each environment finds or creates its own library. One has the packages, the other does not, and `library()` fails on one side only, although the lockfile is the same.

## The fix

Exclude `renv/library` from volumes and images, and restore from the lockfile in each environment.

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```text
# .dockerignore
renv/library
renv/staging
```

```bash
R -e 'renv::restore()'
```
:::
